_readme: Machine-readable catalog of the PRODUCT component library (mirror of components/marketing/catalog.json for the authenticated app). The PreToolUse product-screen-guard injects a digest of this file into every write/edit under app/(dashboard)/** or components/product/**, so the full expressive range of the template is in context on every generation — not just the primitives the model happens to remember. Two kinds of entry: `components` are shared components that already exist in this repo (import them), and `template` are patterns the flyee template ships that have NOT been packaged yet (port them from the cited source instead of inventing a new shape). Keep entries in sync when props change; guard lines render as `Name(props) — use`.
contract: NEVER invent a component. The catalog below is the first stop for any container, tile, card, badge, meter or chart, and it is checked BEFORE markup is written, not after. If nothing here fits, the next stop is the flyee template itself — its dashboard sections are recoverable with `git show "bd92373^:apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/dashboards/..."` — and the new component is PORTED from that source, keeping its shape (radius, tint, band height, type scale), then added to this file in the same commit. Improvising a `<Box>` with a border and a radius is a defect even when it looks acceptable: it type-checks, it passes review, and it quietly grows a second design language beside the template's. `product-lint` blocks the interactive form of this.

Before rendering a value, ask which catalog entry is the right shape for it. A counter set, a ratio, a share and a series each have a component — a run-on sentence of numbers is a defect, not a style.

Never invent a chart to fill space. A visual earns its place only when it answers a question the user actually asks, and only on data the payload already carries. Vanity metrics and decorative charts are forbidden (.claude/rules/app-ux.md).

Never hand-roll a shape that exists here. If the nearest entry does not fit, port the `template` pattern from the cited source (recoverable with `git show "bd92373^:<path>"`) rather than writing a one-off.
Red is reserved for clinical risk and failure. Commercial ceilings, queues and declines use `attention` (accent-3 terracotta) — see usage-meter and library-usage-card for the precedent.
Type scale: body1 14px, body2 12px, subtitle2 14px semibold, h5 18px, h4 20px. `caption` is below 12px — never for informative text.

tones.rule: Icon containers use TILE_TONE (bg-{tone}-light/10 + text-{tone}), tones primary | secondary | accent-1..4. Bars and meters use the UsageMeter vocabulary: primary | secondary | attention | empty. Status labels use the pastel badge, never colour alone.

components.name: EmptyState
components.props: icon?, illustration? (an @/icons/illustrations/* element), title, description?, action?, secondaryAction?, className?, titleAs? (h2 | h3 | h4), layout? (stack | row), framed?
components.use: Every zero-data view: what is empty + why + the ONE next action. Never a bare 'no data'. A section or a list with nothing in it is never left as empty space (the owner, 2026-11-09): give it an `illustration` (the template's line drawings in @/icons/illustrations, drawn in the secondary hue, with the nudge outlined), `layout="row"` for a short band across the page and `framed={false}` inside a card or a grid that frames it already; inside a card whose title is the h2, pass titleAs="h3". Pick the drawing by the subject, one per region of a screen: accounts for people (the patient list), launch for the first record (a patient with no consultation), documentation for papers and a search with no result (the library, the acervo, protocols), storage for what is archived or cancelled, platforms for the calendar (the agenda, the week), integrate for connected apps. A state of permission, of something unavailable or of a failed read keeps its `icon`. The empty state is where a definition teaches: what a section is may be said in full here, and only behind an "i" once it holds something.

components.name: UsageMeter
components.props: headline, caption?, segments[{key,label,value,display,tone}], ariaLabel
components.use: A consumption readout — used vs remaining, with each pool NAMED. Use for any x-of-y allowance (minutes, quota). Beats a plain progress bar when the pools differ in nature (cycle vs purchased).

components.name: MetricBars
components.props: items[{key,label,value,tone?,hint?}], total?, spacing?
components.use: Two to six counters that describe one population (a status funnel, accepted/edited/rejected, failures by stage). Replaces a sentence of counts. Port of the template's Application Status.

components.name: TrendSparkline
components.props: label, data[], plotType?, formatValue?, caption?, tone?
components.use: A SERIES the payload already carries: value + change against the previous point + the curve. Never synthesize a series to decorate. Port of the template's stat-with-sparkline.

components.name: StatTile
components.props: href | onClick+pressed | neither (plain readout), icon, tone, label, value, hint?
components.use: A counter as a tile: tinted icon band (h-[4.5rem]) + label + value in h5, four across. `href` makes it a link; `onClick`+`pressed` make it a real filter button with aria-pressed. Port of dashboard-analytics-stats. A filter row is THIS, never a hand-written Box.

components.name: QuickActionTile
components.props: href, icon, tone, title, description?
components.use: A shortcut: full-height tinted icon column (w-16) + title. Four across, never two columns. A shortcut is its icon and its name (the owner, 2026-11-09): a line under the title only when it says what the name does not (what it unlocks, a state), never one that repeats the name in other words (the home's row has none).

components.name: TILE_TONE
components.props: TILE_TONE[tone] -> { bg, text }
components.use: The only source of icon-container tinting. Never hand-write bg-primary/10 — the template tint is bg-{tone}-light/10.

components.name: ConsultationStatusChip
components.props: status, className?
components.use: A lifecycle stage as the template's pastel badge (Button size=tiny variant=pastel). The pattern to copy for any status label: the state is NAMED, not just coloured.

components.name: ConfirmActionDialog
components.props: title, intro?, consequences[], stays?, staysTitle?, reasonLabel?, reasonPlaceholder?, reasonHelp?, reasonMinLength?, confirmLabel, tone?, onConfirm(reason)->Promise<string|null>, onClose
components.use: Any operator action that changes someone else's account. It forces the three things a confirmation owes the reader: what the action DOES (`consequences`), what it deliberately does NOT do (`stays` — half the risk is assuming it reaches further), and a stated reason for the audit trail. Mount it conditionally with a `key` so it never changes identity on the way out. Never ship a destructive action on a bare click.

components.name: InfoHint
components.props: label, placement?, className?
components.use: What a title, a number or a chip is, behind an "i" a person opens when she wants (a bare Tooltip on a non-focusable Box disappears on touch and for keyboards; this is a real button). 200 characters at most, in every language (kept by lib/i18n/hint-budget.test.ts). SectionTitle and ConsultationStepHeader draw it themselves from their `description`; a page's own h1 puts its definition in one beside it. Never for what must be read before acting: clinical safety text (the PRD §10.11 disclaimer, a draft is not a prescription, a blank field is never a negative), a consequence, a legal note, personal data and the instructions on a patient's own page stay in sight.

components.name: SectionTitle
components.props: id?, title, description? (behind the i), detail? (a line in sight), chip?, action?, as? (h2 | h3 | h4), variant? (h4 | h5 | h6 | subtitle2), className?
components.use: The heading of a section or of a card: its title, what it is FOR behind the "i" beside it (`description`, 200 characters at most), where it stands (`chip`) and its own action at the right (`action`: a button, a progress ring). Never a heading with a paragraph under it read on every visit (the owner, 2026-11-09). `detail` is the one line in sight, only for state or data that tells the thing apart (how many a list holds, who a person is) or for what must be read before acting (a consequence, a legal or clinical safety note, that the AI may err, personal data). A definition that only repeats the title is dropped, and a sentence that says how to use the screen is replaced by what shows it (a chevron, a link). Ported from the sibling platform's SectionTitle; with no CardTitle here, it heads cards too (beside a TILE_TONE icon when the card leads with one).

components.name: ConsultationStepHeader
components.props: step?, icon, title, description? (behind the i), detail? (in sight), status?, statusLabel?, trailing?
components.use: The head of each assistant card of the consultation (record → interpret → plan, and their supporting cards): numbered badge, icon, title and the step's state. When to use the step and what it builds on is `description`, behind the "i"; `detail` stays in sight only for a clinical safety rule or a consequence of acting there (the anamnesis says a blank is never a negative; the hypotheses say tongue and pulse are her observations). One "i" per title: an operational note joins the description instead of a second "i" at the end of the row.

components.name: WeekSchedule
components.props: items, timeZone, locale, agendaHref, scheduleHref, startingId, onStart, onBriefing
components.use: A day strip plus the selected day's items. Port of the template's Schedule card; deliberately NOT the agenda page.

components.name: DataTable
components.props: rows, columns, loading, header?, actions?, filters?, noRowsOverlay, noResultsOverlay, onQuickFilterChange?, initialColumnVisibility?, enableExport?
components.use: The app's ONE table, and only when the job really is scan/compare/manage many rows. Put the page title in `header` and the primary action in `actions` — those slots render empty otherwise. Imports the community DataGrid: pinnedColumns needs the wrapper switched to @mui/x-data-grid-premium (installed and licensed).

components.name: OnboardingChecklist / ActivationProgress / SetupWizard
components.props: see each file
components.use: Steps to first value, completion drive, and progressive disclosure for long setups. Never points, badges, leaderboards or streaks.

components.name: StepCelebrationDialog
components.props: open, title, accomplished, nextTitle, nextHint?, ctaLabel, onNext, onClose
components.use: The beat BETWEEN two steps of a guided flow: names what now exists in her records and loads the next step. Competence feedback, never a token — it awards, counts and ranks nothing, so it stays on the right side of the no-points/badges/leaderboards/streaks rule. Its primary action is what advances the wizard (drive SetupWizard in controlled mode).

components.name: MicCheck
components.props: onResult?(heard | silent | blocked | unavailable)
components.use: 'Will my microphone work?' answered BEFORE a patient is in the room: asks the browser permission, shows the live level and names what it found. Records and uploads nothing. Use wherever the product prepares her for a recording — never as a recorder.

components.name: SignaturePreview
components.props: name, title?, registration?, practiceName?
components.use: The signature block of an issued document as it will print, fed by the same credentialLines() the PDF renderers use. Show it beside any field that changes what goes under her name. A preview of the block only — never mock a document that does not exist.

components.name: FirstConsultationGuide
components.props: withRecording, onStart, onDismiss
components.use: Orientation for a first visit to the consultation screen (what the chief complaint is for, blank = não informado, finalizing freezes). Three facts led by icons, deliberately NOT numbered — the screen numbers its own steps. Guidance about a moment of USE belongs on the screen where it happens, not in the onboarding.

components.name: PracticeModalitiesField
components.props: value, onChange, other, onOtherChange, onBlur?, disabled?, label?, helperText?
components.use: What she treats with: the five product modalities plus her own words. The two lists are stored apart — only the five have clinical effect — and a typed label that names a known modality becomes the known one. The one place the option list and the label rules live.

template.name: Medidor circular (gauge)
template.props: CircularProgress variant="determinate" + centred label + outline-grey-100 track ring
template.use: One ratio that must read at a glance next to its x/y. No chart library. Not packaged yet — port it when a screen needs a single prominent ratio.

template.name: Tile horizontal com variação
template.props: Card flex-row p-1 + Box h-24 w-16 rounded-2xl bg-{tone}-light/10 + label body1 + value h5 + NiTriangleUp/Down change
template.use: A counter that has a previous period to compare against. Requires real prior-period data — otherwise use StatTile.

template.name: Rosca / radar
template.use: Only above ~6 categories, or to compare two comparable series. Below that, MetricBars reads better — prefer it.

template.name: Card ilustrado
template.props: h4 card-title + body1 + Illustration* h-64 max-w-xs + contained/outlined actions
template.use: The zero-data state of a whole screen, when the path to value deserves more than an EmptyState. Packaged example: components/product/home-empty-banner.tsx.

template.name: Timeline de atividade
template.props: @mui/lab Timeline + TimelineDot variant=outlined + subtitle2/body2 + relative time
template.use: 'What happened recently' when the order IS the meaning. Packaged example: the recent-records card in app/(dashboard)/inicio/page.tsx.

traps: MUI 9 builds a component class list as `Mui{Comp}-{variant}` + `Mui{Comp}-color{Color}`; the composed `Mui{Comp}-{variant}{Color}` of MUI 5 is gone. Both known instances are fixed: style/inputs/button.css now targets `.MuiButton-pastel.MuiButton-color{Color}`, and style/data-display/chip.css now targets `.MuiChip-outlined.MuiChip-color{Color}`. An outlined Chip therefore paints BOTH its text (from MUI emotion, matched on props) and its 1px ring (from the template, matched on classes). Before writing a selector against a composed class, check useUtilityClasses in the installed component source — TypeScript will not catch it, because a ChipClasses/ButtonClasses augmentation can declare a class the DOM never receives.
useHighlightedSparkline derives its y-axis from the data: an empty array yields -Infinity. Guard the series before rendering.
The template's `caption` variant is below 12px. Consequence text ('this is recorded with your name') belongs in body2.

An outlined Chip ring inherits the raw colour token, so it is only as legible as that token: on the light theme, error/primary/accent-* clear the 3:1 floor for a graphical object, while info (2.12:1), success (2.13:1), warning (2.51:1) and secondary (2.77:1) do not. Use colour on a Chip as reinforcement of a word that is already in the label, never as the sole carrier of the state.

A colour prop that is CONSTANT down a whole column carries no information and costs contrast: it reads as an affordance (primary) or dilutes the one signal that matters (error). Colour a Chip only where the colour VARIES with the row.

Feedback severity tokens (`--{sev}-light` / `--{sev}-dark`) hold the SAME value in the light and the dark block of design-tokens/css/common.css. A rule written as `text-{sev}-dark` for the light theme is therefore automatically wrong in the dark one, and no `dark:` variant exists to save it. Measured on the Alert: the template pairing of `bg-{sev}-light/10` + `text-{sev}-dark` reads 2.51:1 (info), 2.56:1 (success), 2.95:1 (warning) on light and 2.15:1 for error on dark, against ~9.2:1 for the inherited text. Severity belongs in the BACKGROUND and the ICON; the words keep inheriting text-primary.

The palette is written as `hsl(var(--token))` with cssVariables on. decomposeColor cannot read that and returns NaN WITHOUT throwing, so MUI never reaches its own fallback: every DERIVED colour (theme.alpha, palette.Alert.{sev}StandardBg, getContrastText) resolves to a value the browser discards. Direct references such as palette[sev].main survive — which is why an Alert icon is coloured today while its background is not. Consequence: when a template selector dies there is no native styling underneath it, and any new component that leans on a computed MUI colour is born broken and silent.

Run `npm run check:mui-classes` after touching anything under apps/web/src/style/**. It matches every `.Mui{Comp}-{slot}` against that component's own class manifest in node_modules, the only source of truth: a ChipClasses/ButtonClasses type augmentation can declare a class the DOM never emits, and that is exactly how three stylesheets accumulated dead rules nobody could see.

COLOUR ON A LABEL, MEASURED. This theme's palette is too light on six of its ten colours to carry text, and neither MUI nor the template compensates. Light theme, against the 4.5:1 floor: a FILLED surface (contained Button, filled Chip, Fab, selected ToggleButton) paints the label with `contrastText` = white, which clears only primary 4.89, accent-2 4.51, accent-4 5.22 and error 5.31 — it fails secondary 2.77, accent-1 3.77, accent-3 3.55, info 2.12, warning 2.51, success 2.13. An OUTLINED Chip does NOT rescue it: MUI paints that label `palette[color].main`, the same tone, so outlined warning is also 2.51. The pastel badge is no better (warning 2.95). Only three ways out, in order of preference: fill with one of the four colours that pass; or keep the tone in the RING and give the label `text-text-primary!` (9.79:1), which is what the clinical alert chips in clinical-context-bar.tsx do; or state the severity in the word and drop the colour. Never assume a variant change fixes contrast — measure it.
